text: "Sit at My right hand, till I make Your enemies Your footstool." The Father's order: first rest, then He deals with the enemies.
explanation:
The Father said to the Son, "Sit." Not fight, strive or worry: sit. "Till I make Your enemies Your footstool." And Jesus "must reign till He has put all enemies under His feet. The last enemy that will be destroyed is death." With every passing day, another enemy goes under His feet.

You were raised and seated with Him, so the same order applies to you. When the devil asks, "What are you going to do about this symptom, this debt, this job loss?" answer, "Nothing. I'm seated, and the Father will make it my footstool." Rest isn't inactivity; from rest, the Spirit's promptings become clear. Every fresh challenge calls for a fresh sitting down.

text: "Where is your righteousness?" Look up: there it is, seated at the Father's right hand.
explanation:
John Bunyan once walked through a field, grieving over all the sinful thoughts and tendencies he still found in himself. Suddenly a word came to him: "Your righteousness is in heaven." He looked up and saw by faith Jesus at God's right hand, and realised that his righteousness was there, untouched by his good days or bad ones.

If someone asks whether you're righteous, you can say, "As righteous as Jesus," because He is the measure of your righteousness. God can't remove you from Christ without removing Christ. Your history in Him began at the cross, and you're in Him forever.

text: Solomon's temple chambers were reached by winding stairs. You climb higher, faster, but can't see the end. Take one step at a time.
explanation:
"They went up by winding stairs into the middle story, and from the middle to the third." And each floor was wider than the last: five cubits, six, then seven. A winding stair gains the most height in the least distance, but you can never see the top from where you stand.

During a crisis, God doesn't give you grace to see the ending, and you don't need to dwell on how it began. Like the manna, His grace comes one day at a time. "Since we live by the Spirit, let us keep in step with the Spirit." Do the next thing He shows you. You may not feel it, but you're rising into a wider place.

text: "He will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared." God is bringing you into a place already made ready.
explanation:
Before the Passover, Jesus told two disciples to follow a man carrying a pitcher of water, an unusual sight in a day when women drew the water, and a picture of the Holy Spirit. "He will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us."

It's the same promise God gave Israel: houses you didn't build, wells you didn't dig, vineyards you didn't plant. It means rest through the work of Another. You may not see it with your eyes yet, but your provision is already furnished. "My God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus." Follow the Spirit, and He'll lead you up into it.

text: Law says, "Become what you are not." Grace says, "Become what you already are."
explanation:
Grace has its responsibilities, and the New Testament is full of exhortations. But notice how they're framed: "If then you were raised with Christ, seek those things which are above." "You are complete in Him." "As you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him." Every command starts from what is already true.

Legalism always says, "You're not holy enough yet, so try harder to become something you're not." Grace says, "In God's eyes you're already righteous and complete. Now walk it out": at work, with your spouse, in your family. Walk like the royal child you are.

text: The temple's outer court was always busy; the Holy of Holies was perfectly still. You can be busy outside and at rest inside.
explanation:
You are the temple of God, and the temple had three parts. In the outer court, priests were constantly slaughtering, washing, arranging and clearing ashes: that's your body, busy with daily responsibilities. In the Holy Place, the lamp, the bread and the incense picture your soul, needing light, nourishment and prayer. And in the Holy of Holies, where the ark sat, there was perfect peace: that's your spirit, where Christ dwells.

Rest doesn't mean doing nothing. You can sit perfectly still and have a racing mind; that isn't rest. And you can be fully occupied with work while your spirit is seated in Christ. Do your duties, but don't do them worried.

text: "He was delivered up because of our offenses, and was raised because of our justification." The empty tomb is your receipt.
explanation:
Jesus went to the cross carrying every one of your sins. If His payment had fallen short by a single sin, God could never have raised Him. The resurrection is God's public declaration: the work is perfect, the debt is paid, you are declared righteous.

The same body that bore your sins and carried your diseases at the cross now sits at the Father's right hand, without them. So where are your sins? Gone, forever. And where are the sicknesses He bore? Gone too. Every time you remember that He is risen, remember why: because you've been made right with God.
